title: Insufficient liquidity - the movement would breach Firm B's twelve-month cash reserve
scenarioRefNote: No scenarios.yaml branch covers SINGLE-request reserve insufficiency (the matrix's `competing-liquidity` is the two-request variant, GC-10/GC-11). This case is required by the prompt-2 spec list; it is specified under firm-b because the identical facts PROCEED under firm-a's six-month reserve - the divergence itself is a config-only demo beat.

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. Draft treats reserve insufficiency as a RESOLVABLE block (funds can arrive, pending activity can settle, the amount can shrink), not a prohibition. Re-signed 2026-08-21 under the prompt-5 signature sitting (rulings CD-4c, CD-4b); amendment machine-derived from the generation-4 engine's own evaluation and approved by the captain's merge of the amendment PR.

trigger.description: Advisor enters the $75,000 request; after pending approved activity, liquid assets cannot fund it and preserve twelve months of planned withdrawals.
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD for home-renovation under firm-b reserve policy (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Joint taxable brokerage available balance 160000 USD - the only source that avoids a taxable event.
Pending approved distribution of 20000 USD (already authorized, not yet settled) reduces effective liquidity to 140000 USD.
Planned withdrawals 8000 USD/month; Firm B requires twelve months = 96000 USD in reserve. 140000 - 75000 = 65000 < 96000: the movement would breach the reserve.

householdInstructions.summary: Distributions may only be sent to household-titled bank instructions (satisfied here; liquidity is the failing constraint).
Prefer taxable sources over retirement accounts - which is why the IRA is not offered as an automatic fallback.

expectedAuthority.note: A blocked decision carries no authority and no execution plan (v3 invariant 8). No approver can waive a reserve breach; only changed facts can resolve it.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: Funding 75000 USD from effective liquidity of 140000 USD leaves 65000 USD, below the 96000 USD twelve-month reserve Firm B requires.

blockers.explanation: The movement would leave less than twelve months of planned withdrawals in cash.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: A taxable source account was selected; a retirement account is never chosen silently.
Available 160000 USD minus the pending approved 20000 USD distribution = 140000 USD effective liquidity; pending activity counts against the household (demo-contract household shape).
After the 75000 USD movement only 65000 USD would remain, below Firm B's 96000 USD (twelve-month) reserve - the request blocks with the arithmetic shown.

commentaryNodes.summary: Under Firm A's six-month reserve (48000 USD) the identical facts proceed - the block exists because Firm B's policy version differs, not because the code differs.

commentaryNote: Demoted from the binding explanation set to non-binding commentary by the captain's CD-4b ruling (2026-08-21). Retained as signed intent; describes lifecycle behavior outside the prompt-5 decision engine or comparative context the engine does not emit.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: Balance, pending-action, and planned-withdrawal snapshots pinned into the bundle - the pending 20000 USD activity is part of the recorded basis.
Blocked decision recording the cash-reserve-breach blocker and its resolving evidence; no authority, no execution plan.

expectedVerificationState.note: No execution occurs. The block resolves when fresh evidence shows the reserve satisfied (new funds, settled pending activity, or a smaller request re-entered as a new intent).
